findings.finding: Solstad Maritime's Q3 2026 release (4 Nov) says the high-end North Sea AHTS spot market 'has been solid since Q4'25 with further improvements in Q3'26'. Its three spot/project AHTS ran 89% utilisation in Q3 against 67% in Q2, so Sea1 Ruby, Sea1's one owned North Sea AHTS and largely spot-exposed (AHTS 2026 availability 63% at 30 June), likely had a Q3 at or above its Q2 level.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed record North Sea spot rates (USD 175k/day average) with AHTS revenue up, and the stock fell 1.67% on the day. The AHTS line has not visibly paid on results days.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: on 4 Nov SEA1 rose 2.5% (25.95 to 26.60) alongside SOMA +2.7% and SOFF +4.3%, then gave back 1.1% on 5 Nov. The 2.4-point fall over the prior 20 sessions shows nobody had re-rated Sea1 on the North Sea, and with Q2's sector warning of a 'challenging H2' still the last word, a cleaner Q3 AHTS line is not fully in the price. Net of the rest of the company, the finding is small: Ruby is 1 of 6 owned AHTS and AHTS was 39% of Q2 revenue; Subsea, PSV and FC&OSRV are on firm Brazil contracts and do not move on this.
findings.independence: Sea1's own Q2 market text (AHTS spot tight, rates up 45% q/q) points the same way but is older: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=679773

findings.finding: Australia is softening: Sea1's own Q2 outlook expects 'a further semi-submersible rig decline' there in H2 2026, and Solstad's 4 Nov presentation repeats 'Australia will have lower activity the coming quarters'. Sea1 has two owned AHTS (Sea1 Aquamarine, Sea1 Emerald) and one managed vessel in Australia.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to the Australia line on its own. The Q4 2024 print (-6.9%) and Q2 2025 print (-11.8%) fell on weaker spot and AHTS conditions, but those were not separated by region.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company itself flagged the decline in August and said it 'maintains good contract coverage across the region for most of the year'. So this sits inside what was guided and is sized near 0. It is filed because Solstad's 4 Nov text confirms it persists into the coming quarters, which bears on the outlook paragraph.

findings.finding: Sea1 has filed no contract award or extension on NewsWeb since 16 January 2026 (Sea1 Maragogi). Firm backlog fell from USD 701m to 625m in H1, and Subsea/FC&OSRV are 24% open for 2027, so the Q3 backlog figure probably shows another step down unless the release carries unannounced awards.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog fell from 755.8m to 625m year on year in the Q2 print, and the stock fell 1.67%. No separate measurement exists for this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-off is arithmetic anyone with the Q2 report can do, so most of it is priced. The open question is whether the post-election Petrobras tendering that management expected 'towards the end of the year' has started; the release is the first place that shows up. The 60-day run-up of -11.7% is consistent with the market already leaning on this, which is why it is small.
